reuse.why: Puts the rule in the shared getScheduledAmount, but re-derives the 7.5% tolerance as Math.round(Math.abs(amount) * 0.075) instead of calling the existing getApproxNumberThreshold in shared/rules.ts that the matching code uses.

duplication.why: The approximate tolerance formula now exists in two places (shared/rules.ts getApproxNumberThreshold and shared/schedules.ts getScheduledAmount), so matching and planning can drift apart.

placement.why: The worst-case computation lives in the shared schedules helper next to the ranged rule, which is the right layer; the isapprox detection stays at the caller.

scope.why: Small, focused change: one helper, one call site, one test.

maintainability.why: A boolean positional third parameter after another boolean is easy to misuse, the tolerance is duplicated, and only the forecast caller passes it, so other planning paths (schedule-template, preview transactions, balances) silently keep the exact value.

bypasses_abstraction.where: shared/schedules.ts getScheduledAmount inlines the 0.075 tolerance instead of using getApproxNumberThreshold from shared/rules.ts.

disguised_duplication.where: getApproxNumberThreshold's Math.round(Math.abs(n) * 0.075) is re-inlined inside the approximate branch of getScheduledAmount rather than called.

one_place.where: Only forecast-schedules.ts normalizeSchedule passes approximate=true; schedule-template.ts, the preview path in shared/schedules.ts, schedules/app.ts and the client balance/list callers of getScheduledAmount still use the exact value, and the tolerance itself is defined twice.
